caption: Is Jesus the commander who met Joshua? The theological link is possible, but Hebrews never cites the story—and the apparent word match depends on English translation.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Is Jesus Joshua’s commander? Joshua meets the commander of the LORD’s army. Hebrews calls Jesus the leader—or pioneer—of salvation.
slides.body: Joshua meets the commander of the LORD’s army. Hebrews calls Jesus the leader—or pioneer—of salvation.
slides.heading: Is Jesus Joshua’s commander?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Josh 5:14-15: I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.
slides.body: I have now come as Commander of the LORD’s army.
slides.heading: Josh 5:14-15

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Heb 2:10, BSB: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.
slides.body: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Heb 2:10

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them Joshua’s commander stands on holy ground. Some Christians identify him as the divine Son before Jesus’s birth.
slides.body: Joshua’s commander stands on holy ground. Some Christians identify him as the divine Son before Jesus’s birth.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the words are different Joshua and Hebrews use different Greek terms, and Hebrews never mentions this story. “Captain” makes the link look closer in English.
